business_scope.primary_industry_name: Administration of Employee Share Incentive Plans (ESOP Trusts)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley 526 de 1999 (Financial Information and Anti-Money Laundering legal framework), Ley 1121 de 2007, Ley 1621 de 2013, Decreto 1067 de 2015, Ley 2010 de 2019, Decreto 830 de 2021, and Regulatory Resolution 000080 of 2023 (DIAN) establishing the Registro Único de Beneficiarios Finales (RUB) and mandatory UBO disclosure obligations.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified Copy of Passport of Each Shareholder and Legal Representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National Authority of Country of Origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation and Good Standing of Corporate Shareholder (if applicable)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent Company Registry of Country of Origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Duly Notarized Power of Attorney for Incorporation Filings
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public in Country of Origin or Colombian Notary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Colombian Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter and Source of Funds Certificate for Initial Capital Contributions
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed Financial Institution in the Country of Origin

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all prospective shareholders, ultimate beneficial owners, directors, and legal representatives against the OFAC SDN List, United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, Colombian 'Lista Clinton' (DAS/UNP), and domestic PEP registers as administered by the Colombian Superintendence of Companies and UIAF, in accordance with Circular Externa 003 de 2020 and the SAGRILAFT compliance regime.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Único Empresarial y Social (RUES) — www.rues.org.co
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: All corporate names must be submitted in Spanish. Non-Spanish words must be transliterated into Spanish script or accompanied by a certified translation. Names must include a distinctive element followed by 'S.A.S.' and may not be identical, confusingly similar, or phonetically equivalent to an existing registered trademark or corporate name in the Cámara de Comercio database.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the name reservation is rejected, the applicant may file a writ of reconsideration ('recurso de reposición') before the relevant Cámara de Comercio within 10 business days of notification, followed if necessary by a subsidiary appeal ('recurso de apelación') before the Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio within 5 business days. A complete re-application with a new distinctive name is also permissible after the rejection decision.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for an S.A.S. engaged in ESOP trust administration, provided a physical domicile is designated for service of process in Colombia. A virtual office may be used where no regulated sector activity is carried out, but the registered address must appear in the RUES registry and accept official notices.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name availability search and homonymy certificate at Cámara de Comercio
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá / Local Chamber of Commerce
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff schedule for registry services

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: S.A.S. incorporation registration fee (commonly referred to as 'Cámara de Comercio filing fee')
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff based on transaction value and corporate asset size

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization fee for private incorporation document and shareholder resolutions
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notarial tariff (Decreto 960 de 1970 and amendments)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Hague Apostille authentication for foreign natural person and corporate shareholders' documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the relevant country of origin
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Consular or apostille fixed fee per document

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal drafting of S.A.S. bylaws, ESOP trust administration provisions, and UBO disclosure declarations
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for multinational low-risk incorporation services

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registro Único de Beneficiarios Finales (RUB) initial filing
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: DIAN — Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory administrative fee for UBO registry

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RUT tax registration and DIAN digital certificate (Certificado Digital de Firma Electrónica)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory administrative fee for tax registration and digital certification

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: PEP, OFAC, UN, and domestic sanctions screening of all UBOs and legal representatives
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for per-entity screening subscription or one-time due diligence package

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office / virtual office service for the first year

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for commercial registered address service

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley 1258 de 2008 ('Por medio de la cual se crea la sociedad por acciones simplificada'), Articles 1-50; Código de Comercio (Decreto 410 de 1971), Articles 98, 110-119, 353-373 (residual application); Decreto 1074 de 2015, Title II (commercial registry and Chamber of Commerce functions); Ley 1780 de 2016 (simplified virtual incorporation window for small entities).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cámara de Comercio with territorial jurisdiction over the registered office (e.g., Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá), operating the Registro Único Empresarial y Social (RUES) under the functional supervision of the Superintendencia de Sociedades; DIAN assigns the NIT and maintains the Registro Único Tributario (RUT).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Documento Privado de Constitución of the S.A.S. (or Escritura Pública No. [●] if real property is contributed or notarial formality is voluntarily adopted), inscribed in the Registro Mercantil via the RUES.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No legal minimum capital; the S.A.S. may be constituted with one (1) share of nominal value (as low as one COP). Subscribed capital may be paid in cash, in kind, or by set-off, with payment terms freely fixed in the bylaws. No compulsory escrow account is required by Ley 1258/2008; escrow is only advisable for foreign-currency contributions, which must be channeled through authorized foreign-exchange intermediaries in accordance with the Colombian exchange regime.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED BY THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [●] S.A.S.: FIRST: Ratify the subscription of [●] ordinary nominative shares, fully paid, representing one hundred percent of the authorized capital. SECOND: Adopt as registered office the principal place of administration at [●], Bogotá D.C., Colombia, and instruct the legal representative to file the address before the Chamber of Commerce and DIAN. THIRD: Appoint [●] as Legal Representative and [●] as Secretary, each accepting office under the bylaws. FOURTH: Authorize the opening of the corporate bank account and signing of the commercial registration forms. Certified this [date] by the Secretary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate name availability pre-validation and reservation before the Chamber of Commerce
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio del domicilio principal (e.g., Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá) via the RUES virtual portal (www.rues.org.co), Registro Mercantil section.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Access the Chamber/RUES virtual platform (Ventanilla Única Empresarial), file the homonymy and name availability inquiry ('consulta de homonimia') with the proposed corporate name; obtain the certificate of name availability ('Certificado de Homónimos'); reserve the selected name for the statutory 30-day term; pay the nominal search fee by PSE electronic bank transfer.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name (up to three alternatives)
Valid identity document (cédula/passport) of the requesting shareholder or attorney-in-fact
Corporate email address
PSE payment receipt for the name reservation fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for homonymy with an existing legal entity, file a new consultation with a different name at no additional substantive cost; a single extension of the reservation term may be requested through the portal before expiry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the incorporation instrument (Documento Privado de Constitución S.A.S.)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Shareholders directly, or a Notaría (Notaría Única / notaries of the circuit) if real property is contributed or if the parties elect notarial formality.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the S.A.S. bylaws under Ley 1258/2008, covering corporate name, domicile, term of duration, corporate purpose (expressly including 'administration of employee share incentive plans and ESOP trusts'), authorized, subscribed, and paid capital, board and legal representative powers, shareholder meeting rules, and arbitration/conflict clauses; execute the document by all subscribing shareholders, or by the sole shareholder if a single-member S.A.S.; if notarized, obtain the corresponding Escritura Pública.
required_dossiers: Draft S.A.S. bylaws (documento privado de constitución)
Valid identity documents of all incorporating shareholders (cédula or passport)
Certificate of name availability (Certificado de Homónimos) within its 30-day validity
Minutes of the constitutive shareholders' meeting or unanimous written consent adopting the First Board Resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Chamber or notary detects an illegal clause, irregular capital computation, or defective purpose description, amend the incorporation document by a signed reform (reforma al documento privado) and resubmit; notarial corrections follow the notary's redarguy procedure at no additional registry cost beyond corrected pages.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial registration and issuance of the Certificado de Cámara de Comercio
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio del domicilio principal — Registro Mercantil; integrated with DIAN through RUES for automatic NIT assignment.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the executed incorporation document together with the RUES registration forms (Formulario de Registro Único Empresarial y Social and, if applicable, the establecimiento de comercio form) at the Chamber counters or through the virtual window; the Chamber verifies legal conformity, inscribes the company and its legal representative, assigns the matrícula mercantil number, issues the 'certificado de existencia y representación legal', and transmits the registration record to DIAN, which automatically assigns the NIT.
required_dossiers: Documento Privado de Constitución (original and copy)
Certificate of name availability
Formulario RUES de registro de sociedad
Acceptance letter of the legal representative and secretary
Bank receipt or PSE proof of the Chamber registration fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is suspended by a written observation, the legal representative must cure the defect within 20 business days by submitting corrected documentation; if the NIT is not auto-generated within RUES, the representative must attend DIAN with the Chamber certificate to obtain the NIT and RUT password manually.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax registration (RUT/NIT) before DIAN and activation of electronic invoicing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN) — Registro Único Tributario (RUT) and facturación electrónica portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The legal representative logs into the DIAN virtual office (sede electrónica), validates the assigned NIT, confirms the RUT with the relevant tax responsibilities ('01' income tax, '05' VAT, '20' withholding agent status as applicable), obtains the electronic signature (firma electrónica), and enrolls in the mandatory electronic invoicing system so that no paper invoices are issued; the company must thereafter keep the RUT updated in the Diamond/consultation portal.
required_dossiers: Certificado de Cámara de Comercio (not older than 30 days)
Identity document and RUT of the legal representative
Corporate email and mobile phone number
Copy of the bylaws (if requested by DIAN)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If DIAN queries the RUT update, correct the data through the online 'Actualización del RUT' form and retransmit; if the digital password is lost, recover it via the DIAN virtual procedure or attend a physical DIAN service point with certified corporate documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate governance book setup and ESOP administrative trust documentation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate organs (shareholders and board); registrations before the Superintendencia de Sociedades for bylaws and governance; Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio (SIC) for personal-data registry if employee data is processed.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open the shareholder ledger (libro de registro de accionistas) and minutes book (libro de actas) in accordance with the Commercial Code; implement the ESOP incentive trust structure: execution of the trust agreement, share subscription and transfer schedules, vesting calendars, and payroll deduction authorizations; keep the stock-plan documentation in the corporate books and, where employee personal data is processed, file the database registration (Registro Nacional de Bases de Datos) with SIC under Law 1581 of 2012.
required_dossiers: First Board Resolution and share subscription minutes
Shareholder register and initial share transfer record
ESOP trust agreement and plan rules (drafts or executed copies)
SIC database registration form and data-processing consent template
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Corporate governance gaps are cured by an extraordinary shareholders' meeting ratifying prior managerial acts (confirmación de gestiones); SIC queries are remedied by filing an updated privacy policy and production of employee consent records within the statutory response term.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal, occupational, and physical-premises licensing (if an office is opened)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alcaldía Mayor / Secretaría Distrital de Hacienda for ICA municipal tax registration; Cuerpo Oficial de Bomberos for the fire-safety certificate; Secretaría Distrital de Planeación for land-use conformity.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the economic activity (CIIU 6430) with the municipal treasury for the industry and commerce tax (ICA) regime, whether by declaration or annual fixed tariff; obtain the Certificado de Bomberos for the physical office; implement the Sistema de Gestión de Seguridad y Salud en el Trabajo (SG-SST) under Resolution 0312 of 2019 and affiliate employees with ARL, EPS, and pension funds; verify that the lease complies with local land-use rules (uso de suelo) before occupying the premises.
required_dossiers: Certificado de Cámara de Comercio
RUT with ICA municipal registration evidence
Lease agreement for the registered office
SG-SST implementation matrix and ARL employee affiliation forms
Fire-safety certificate (Certificado de Bomberos) for the premises
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the fire-safety or land-use certificate is withheld, correct the physical conditions (extinguishers, emergency signage, structural loads, or zoning use) and request re-inspection; ICA registration objections may be appealed to the municipal tax authority within 30 days of notice.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — no manufacturing or industrial transformation activity under ISIC 6430; reference authority for municipal land use and commercial-office compliance: Secretaría Distrital de Planeación / Alcaldía Local of the registered office.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No sectoral operating permit is imposed on an S.A.S. ESOP administrative trust; ordinary commercial registration (matrícula mercantil) and municipal commercial-establishment registration (matrícula de establecimiento de comercio) suffice for a physical office.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Autoridad Nacional de Licencias Ambientales (ANLA) for national-level EIA; Secretaría Distrital de Ambiente (SDA) for local office-related environmental matters — neither is triggered by administrative trust activity.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — purely administrative and fiduciary activity; no Category I–III industrial activity, no quarrying, no hazardous operations, and no significant resource consumption.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial discharge or VOC emission limits apply; if a physical office exists, general compliance with Decreto 1076 de 2015 (environmental code) and Resolución 631 de 2015 (sewer discharge limits) is limited to ordinary sanitary wastewater, while solid waste is handled under municipal solid-waste tariffs and recycling ordinances.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Certificado de Bomberos (fire-safety certificate) required for the physical office; compliance with structural and seismic design standards of Ley 400 de 1997 and NSR-10 for load-bearing capacity; implementation of the SG-SST occupational health management system per Resolución 0312 de 2019; mandatory ARL employee enrolment before any economic activity commences at the premises.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN), Colombian national tax and customs authority; official portal: www.dian.gov.co (and the MUISCA electronic system for registration and filings)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity establishing a Colombian S.A.S. must appoint a resident legal representative and execute the incorporation deed (Escritura Pública or Private Document) before a notary, followed by registration in the Cámara de Comercio. The Registro Único Tributario (RUT) must then be obtained online via DIAN's MUISCA portal. The DIAN assigns the Número de Identificación Tributaria (NIT) upon RUT approval. For foreign entities without a local branch, a NIT may be obtained for indirect tax purposes using a local authorized attorney-in-fact with a power of attorney, but the standard route for an operational Colombian S.A.S. is statutory incorporation and RUT issuance. After RUT activation, the entity must obtain an electronic signature certificate (Certificado de Firma Electrónica) from an authorized provider to submit VAT and income tax returns.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; the Colombian S.A.S. is a separate juridical person taxed as a national corporation under Colombian income tax law (Estatuto Tributario). Colombia does not recognize check-the-box pass-through treatment for S.A.S. entities; profits are subject to corporate income tax at the entity level, and dividends are separately taxed at shareholder level when distributed. Territorial scope applies to Colombian-source income, with broad foreign-source income taxation for resident entities per ordinary residence rules.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-type check-the-box election exists. The S.A.S. by law is always a taxable corporation (sociedad comercial) and cannot elect to be treated as transparent or as a branch for tax purposes. Hybrid mismatch elections are not generally available; Colombia implements anti-hybrid rules under the OECD/G20 Inclusive Framework (Law 2277 of 2022), but these operate as disallowance rules rather than elective classifications. Certain new companies may elect the 'sociedad beneficiosa e innovadora' (SOCIEDAD BIC) regime, which grants tax benefits, and the S.A.S. may elect progressive tax rate banding only in respect of small-business thresholds under Article 242 of the Tax Code, but this is not an entity-classification election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Impuesto sobre las ventas (IVA) — Colombian value-added tax (VAT). Also applies national consumption tax on certain services (impuesto al consumo) and municipal industry and commerce tax (ICA) at territorial level. For ESOP trust administration services, VAT generally applies at the standard rate on services rendered in the national territory.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Responsible entities must register in the RUT as IVA-responsible persons. There is no general economic turnover threshold: any person engaged in taxable activities, importing goods, or contracting taxable services is obliged to register. Optional simplified registration applies only to small traders under Article 437 of the Tax Statute, subject to gross income below COP 3,500,000 per year and other conditions. An S.A.S. operating a commercial trust administration service will almost always exceed the nominal threshold and must register. For goods importers, registration is mandatory irrespective of value.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Colombia mandates structured electronic invoicing (factura electrónica) through DIAN's electronic invoicing platform (Actividad de Facturación Electrónica). The issuer must transmit XML invoices to DIAN in real time and receive a valid electronic acceptance (CUNE) using the DIAN-enabled computer system or authorized software. For international transactions, the equivalent is the electronic dispatch document ('documento equivalente') for non-invoice operations. Export invoices must be digitally endorsed. DIAN uses the electronic billing exchange (Sistema de Facturación Electrónica) with validation of CUNE codes and the export declaration is reported in the electronic system. Qualified electronic signatures are mandatory; there is no physical stamp, but clearance is denied if the XML fails DIAN's real-time validation.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods permanently exported are zero-rated under Article 481 of the Tax Statute, provided they leave the country within the terms of the customs regime. Export of services to non-residents is also zero-rated if the service is wholly performed abroad or the recipient is a foreign entity without domicile in Colombia, subject to compliance with Article 481(d) and the regulatory regime of Decree 2090 of 2017. For an ESOP trust, administrative services rendered to a foreign beneficiary or foreign company may be zero-rated if the service is not connected to Colombian assets and the recipient is located overseas. The trust must demonstrate the service is exported and not used domestically. The entity must be an IVA-responsible registered VAT taxpayer. Zero-rating does not require a formal prior approval but is applied on the export invoice; refund of VAT credits arises through the periodic VAT returns.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Formulario Único de Exportación (DEX) approved by DIAN or the authorized customs broker
Bill of Lading (Cartas de Porte/Conocimiento de Embarque) or airway bill for goods; for services, the service contract and export certificate issued under Article 481(d)
Commercial Invoice and Export Invoice (Factura de Exportación) with electronic validation
Inward Remittance Certificate (Certificado de compensación de divisas) issued by the Colombian intermediary bank or sociedades corredoras de cambio showing repatriation of export proceeds
Proof of customs export declaration (Export Definitiva) stamped by DIAN customs authority
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DIAN may deny zero-rated treatment if the exporter fails to prove physical exit of goods or true rendering of services to a foreign beneficiary. Fraudulent zero-rating triggers retrospective tax assessment with the maximum penalty for misdeclaration under Article 648 of the Tax Statute, equal to 200% of the tax assessed, plus interest accruing from the demand date. Additional penalties for inaccurate or false export documentation under customs law (Decreto 1165 of 2019) include fines of up to COP 18,000,000, seizure of goods, and criminal fraud sanctions under Law 1762 of 2015 (customs fraud) if evidence suggests intentional evasion. If the export proceeds are not received within the 180-day deadline, or the inward remittance certificate is missing, DIAN may claw back the VAT differential, and for services, the zero-rating is disallowed entirely. The entity bears the burden of proof; mere invoice issuance without bank certificate and customs validation is insufficient.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de la República de Colombia (Central Bank of Colombia) acting as the primary monetary and foreign exchange authority, together with the Comité de Cambios for exchange control policy and the Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia for banking and financial supervision.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Colombia operates a conditional free-convertibility regime. Current account transactions are freely convertible and must be routed through authorized foreign exchange intermediaries or registered foreign currency accounts. Capital account transactions, including inbound foreign direct investment and outbound disbursements, require registration with the Banco de la República’s Sistema de Información Cambiaria (Foreign Exchange Information System) but generally do not require prior exchange control authorization. Profit remittances are permissible after the foreign investment is duly registered, the dividend distribution is legally approved, all Colombian corporate income tax obligations are settled, and applicable dividend withholding taxes are satisfied. Practical hurdles include incomplete registration of the beneficial ownership chain, tax non-deductibility of certain expenditures, and AML/KYC verification of the ultimate trust beneficiaries.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Exporters of goods and services must channel export proceeds through the official foreign exchange market or a registered foreign exchange account. The statutory settlement term is generally six months from the contractual payment due date, not exceeding six months from the date of shipment or provision of the service. There is no mandatory conversion ratio into Colombian pesos; the exporter may hold and use the foreign currency, provided the exchange declaration (Form Declaración de Cambio) is timely filed and evidence of repatriation is retained. Extensions are available upon prior Banco de la República authorization, and non-compliance triggers fines, sanctions, and foreign exchange tax adjustments.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore digital EMIs (Electronic Money Institutions) have limited viability in Colombia. They may establish correspondent or settlement relationships with locally licensed banks, but they cannot accept client deposits or operate as clearing institutions without obtaining a Colombian financial license from the Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia. Viability rating: Medium for inbound international remittances and card payouts through local partner banks; Low for fiduciary ESOP administration where licensed asset custody and Colombian-seated trust accounts are required. Transactions in Colombian pesos must settle through the local ACH/CUD infrastructure; offshore EMIs cannot independently interface with Banco de la República’s settlement systems.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Colombian AML regulations generally require the legal representative and the ultimate beneficial owners of the corporate client to complete a KYC interview with the bank’s compliance officer. In practice, at least one director with express authority must attend a physical meeting at the branch or, in some cases, a certified video conference using secure digital channels. Non-resident directors must provide apostilled and notarized corporate authorizations, passport copies, and a local power of attorney to the Colombian bank representative. Remote opening is not widely permitted for non-residents; the dominant standard is a physical or dual-digital appearance for all signatories and display of original or apostilled constituent documents.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership ambiguity arising from the ESOP trust structure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified trust deed, ESOP plan rules, register of beneficiaries with national tax IDs, board resolutions authorizing the trust, source-of-funds declaration, and organizational chart identifying each ultimate beneficial owner and their proportionate control rights.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk jurisdiction nexus for grantors, foreign employees, or transferring shareholders
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apostilled corporate registries, sanctions and PEP screening reports for all named beneficial owners, independent audit letter confirming the ESOP’s economic substance, and sworn statements explaining the business rationale for foreign participation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual transaction profile involving frequent, high-value distributions without corresponding commercial invoices
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Digital copies of employment agreements, stock option grant notices, vesting schedules, board minutes declaring dividends or share redemptions, formal treasury policy, and third-party valuation reports or transfer pricing documentation supporting the disbursement amounts.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound shareholder contributions into the Colombian ESOP trust must be remitted via SWIFT MT103 from the foreign parent or investors to the S.A.S.’s operational or capital escrow account at an authorized local bank. The wire must clearly state the foreign investment purpose code (Inversión directa para desarrollo de la empresa en Colombia), the investor’s registration number, and the beneficiary account number. The transaction must be accompanied by a board resolution, updated corporate purpose, valuation letter for shares or capital contribution, and be registered with Banco de la República within 30 business days. Foreign currency received in Colombia must be sold to the local market or maintained in a registered foreign currency account within the permitted limits. Capital increases are allowed without prior authorization but require submission of the corresponding exchange declaration and ensuing investment registration.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For ESOP trust distributions, beneficiary payouts, and third-party service settlements, the primary outbound rails are SWIFT MT103 wires through the Banco de la República electronic foreign exchange system, commercial letters of credit for trade payables, and local ACH/CUD transfers for COP disbursements. Each outbound operation must include the standard recipient bank’s SWIFT/BIC, the beneficiary legal name and tax ID, an accurate exchange declaration code for the underlying operation, and a certificate of tax withholding. USD settlements to foreign beneficiaries clear through correspondent banks using CHIPS or Fedwire, while EUR and GBP flows use SEPA/TARGET2 via the local bank’s international correspondent network. All outbound payments require the maintenance of underlying documentation for at least five years.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: COP/USD forward contracts (contratos forward) traded through authorized local financial institutions and custodians
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on COP/USD offshore, available through foreign counterparties with Banco de la República registration and actual delivery limitations stated at inception
Currency swaps (swaps de monedas) involving COP and hard currencies, executed only with licensed local banks or supervised foreign counterparties and registered where required

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Renovación de la Matrícula Mercantil — annual renewal of the commercial registration of the S.A.S.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cámara de Comercio of the registered office (e.g., Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá for a Bogotá-domiciled entity).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Between 1 January and 31 March each year, based on the commercial register status as of 31 December of the previous year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Variable chamber tariff based on total assets; delayed renewal triggers a late-renewal penalty, and repeated non-renewal can lead to cancellation of the mercantile registration, suspension of commercial activity, and administrative deregistration of the entity.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: SAS entities are taxed at the standard 35% headline rate. No blanket tax holiday applies to ESOP administration companies in Colombia. Relevant incentives include: (i) deduction for actual employee stock award costs and cash-settled share plan liabilities when paid; (ii) VAT exemption on exported administrative services where the Colombian SAS renders ESOP administration services to a foreign plan sponsor; (iii) income tax credit for training expenditure up to 10% of payroll where applicable; and (iv) occasional gains tax at 15% on capital gains from share revaluation, replacing ordinary CIT on that gain. These incentives do not change the statutory 35% rate unless a specific, registered, and economically substantive activity is proven to DIAN.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 210 - Declaración de Renta y Complementarios; filed electronically through DIAN portal (Muisca/Ventanilla Electrónica).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Calendar-year taxpayers must file according to the DIAN schedule issued each March-April based on the last two digits of the NIT. The deadline may not extend beyond four months after the fiscal year-end (usually April of the following year).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross ordinary and non-operating revenue: ESOP administration fees, interest on plan assets, share transfer gains.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only Colombian-source income. If services are rendered from Colombia to a foreign plan sponsor, treat as export service income; if a fixed place of business exists abroad, assess permanent establishment exposure.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Direct costs of plan administration, custody, payroll, and deductions for share-based compensation actually transferred to beneficiary employees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deductions require payroll records and social security contributions when beneficiaries are Colombian residents; foreign beneficiaries are not subject to Colombian payroll but must be proved by board minutes and trust deed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Preliminary net taxable income after costs and deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign shareholders should allocate Colombian-source expenses in proportion to ownership; expenses allocable to exempt export services must be separated.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable net income after applying the 5-year tax loss carryforward; annual offset limited to 25% of the pre-offset profit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Carryforward losses must have been filed in a prior return and remain within the eligible 5-year period for 2024-2029 losses.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax rate applied to the SAS.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: 35% flat rate applies to all taxpaying entities, including non-resident owned SAS; no preferential rate for foreign investors without a DTA.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Basic CIT liability: 35% x taxable net income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Creditable foreign tax on the same income may be claimed if a DTA is in force; withhold dividend tax on any deemed distribution.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: CIT plus occasional gains tax (15% on capital gains from share transfers and liquidations not treated as ordinary income).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Equity transferred to employees at less than fair market value may trigger an occasional gains tax event; ensure valuation report is attached.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Prepaid tax, withholding credits, and estimated payments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident withholding certificates must be issued in the name of the SAS; foreign tax credits require authentic documentation and translation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 180 - Saldo a pagar / saldo a favor
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final net CIT payable or carryforward credit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The non-resident legal representative must hold an NIT and electronic signature; wire payments in USD are converted at the official exchange rate.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: monthly surcharge of 1% of total tax assessment, capped at 100%, plus daily interest at DIAN rates. If no tax is payable, a fixed sanction of approximately COP 1.5-5.5 million applies per month. Incomplete return: applicable fine from 5% to 15% of assessed taxes, subject to aggravated penalties for falsification.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 120 - Informe de Operaciones con Vinculadas del Exterior; transmitted electronically with XML annexes to DIAN.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filed together with the annual CIT return, subject to DIAN scheduling; large taxpayers file in June-August following the fiscal year-end, all taxpayers by December 31 of the following calendar year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: List of related parties, tax residency, and group shareholding structure.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Every foreign shareholder owning 10% or more, or exercising management control over the ESOP trustee, must be identified.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: All transactions with foreign related parties by nature (administrative services, financing, intangibles, dividends, share transfers).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The transfer of ESOP shares to a foreign parent at nil value is a reportable transaction even if no consideration changes hands.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciliation of operating margin, EBIT, and net margin with financial statements and comparable benchmarks.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a single-entity ESOP administrator, TNMM with regional compensation comparables normally applies; CUP may be used if identical plan administration fees are offered to unrelated parties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statement of treaty relief claimed in the CIT return and corresponding payee certification.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A certificate of tax residence from the foreign jurisdiction must be appended; without it, treaty relief cannot be applied.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or non-filing: fine of 2%-20% of the omitted related-party transaction amounts; failure to produce supporting documentation may attract fines up to 10,000 UVT (approximately COP 470 million at 2025 UVT); adjustments may add the differential tax plus a 100% penalty.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 7.5% final withholding tax on dividends paid to non-residents out of fully taxed Colombian-source profits; 10% is withheld on the portion of dividends paid out of profits not subject to the standard 35% CIT (e.g. exempt income or special regime profits).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To apply a reduced DTA rate (generally 0-15% depending on ownership), the non-resident shareholder must deliver before payment: (i) a certificate of tax residence (TRC) for the relevant fiscal year; (ii) a completed DIAN form for treaty benefits (provided through the tax portal); (iii) evidence of shareholding percentage and holding period; and (iv) a board resolution of the SAS confirming the beneficiary ownership. The paying entity must retain these documents for at least five years and file the treaty claim in the annual CIT return. If the TRC is defective, the statutory 7.5% or 10% rate must be applied provisionally; a refund application may be filed later through DIAN formal ruling procedures.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest paid to foreign related parties is subject to 15% withholding tax, reduced to 0-10% under applicable DTA. Royalties and IP license fees paid abroad are subject to 15% withholding tax at the statutory rate, commonly reduced to 10% or 12% by tax treaties when the beneficial owner meets limitation-on-benefits clauses. Payments for technical assistance outside a licensed IP arrangement attract 15% WHT as service income; pure offshoring fees are not automatically exempt from Colombian-source characterization if the payor is entitled to an expense deduction in Colombia.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Form 120 and disclosure are mandatory if gross ordinary income exceeds COP 135,000 UVT (approximately COP 6.4 billion at 2025 UVT) or if cross-border related-party transactions exceed COP 10,000 UVT. A full Local File must be prepared and filed when gross revenues exceed COP 450,000 UVT or related-party cross-border transactions exceed COP 20,000 UVT. A Master File is required at the group level if consolidated group revenue exceeds COP 4 million UVT. Even where no filing threshold is met, transfer pricing principles apply to the ESOP trustee for services and share transfers with the foreign grantor or parent.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Colombia does not apply Gulf-style Economic Substance Regulations, but DIAN and the Superintendence of Companies enforce substance-over-form tests under the Tax Code and Company Law. An ESOP trust administered by a SAS must show real local presence: employees, premises, board minutes, service contracts, trust accounting, and independent decision documents. Missing substance will lead to recharacterization as a shell company, automatic denial of DTA benefits, attribution of undistributed profits to foreign owners, and application of the 10% surcharge sanction regime.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax evasion through sham trust and mischaracterized dividends
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Creating a SAS ESOP trustee with no economic activity while the foreign parent or ultimate grantor exercises complete control and receives dividends or share appreciation benefits without declaring them; accounting records manipulate book value to avoid dividend WHT; no actual ESOP beneficiaries or vesting documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DIAN reassessment at the shareholder level, imposing the ordinary 35% CIT plus dividend WHT at 7.5%/10%; accuracy penalty of 100%-200% of the omitted tax (Tax Code Articles 647-648). Criminal evasion is punishable with imprisonment of 48-108 months (Criminal Code Article 287).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false returns are jointly and severally liable for the unpaid tax; assets may be attached, a travel ban may be ordered, and imprisonment is possible if criminal intent is established.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer pricing non-disclosure and falsified valuation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to file Form 120 or prepare a Local File although cross-border related-party transactions exceed the UVT threshold; recording ESOP share transfers at zero value; using non-arm's length administrative fees and lacking margin comparability with Latin American compensation and benefit administration peers.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DIAN may adjust taxable income to the arm's length result, charge 35% tax on the adjustment, apply monthly interest, and impose a fine up to 100% of the adjusted amount; failure to present documentation may attract fines up to 10,000 UVT and loss of treaty benefits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable for the additional tax and interests if willful concealment is proven; the veil of the SAS can be pierced under Law 1258/2008, and directors can face criminal liability for falsifying transfer pricing certificates.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the ESOP trust to disguise politically exposed persons (PEP) or hidden grantors; failing to identify ultimate beneficiaries in the annual beneficial ownership declaration to DIAN; moving share capital or dividends in cash-like instruments through rapid wire transfers without UIAF suspicious transaction reports.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Monetary fines up to 1,200 SMMLV (minimum legal monthly wage) under Law 526/1999; freezing of bank accounts and share registers; cancellation of the company registration if the entity is classified as a money-laundering conduit; confiscation of shares involved in illicit operations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managing directors face criminal prosecution for money laundering under Criminal Code Article 323 (imprisonment of 10-25 years), personal asset confiscation, disqualification from commercial activities, and travel bans during investigation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unreported foreign shareholders and undocumented DTA claims
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Applying a zero or lower dividend withholding rate to a related shareholder in a DTA jurisdiction without obtaining a valid TRC; omitting the ultimate controlling party from the country-by-country report; deducting ESOP stock compensation when the shares were never delivered to employee beneficiaries and the trust deed is undated or inconsistent with payroll data.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The withholding agent is assessed for 7.5% or 10% on gross dividends, plus a 100% penalty for incorrect completed tax returns; the false share-based compensation deduction triggers a 35% surtax, indexing, and infraction fines; in serious cases the company license may be suspended.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable for unpaid withholding taxes and jointly liable for civil restitution when the SAS lacks sufficient assets; criminal charges for false certification are possible if a TRC is fabricated; travel bans and asset freezes are common prior to trial.
